text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A presidential task force has been inaugurated to investigate recurring bomb attacks on military targets, says army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Felix Chukwuma.
- Demand for foreign exchange at weekly auction falls to $70.76 million this week from $90.36 million last week.
- State oil company NNPC plans to reduce its operational costs by trimming expenses on chemical catalysts used at its refineries and petrochemical plants.
- Aviation minister says no to plan by local airline operators to increase domestic air fares by 200 percent.
- Stock exchange suspends broker over fictitious transaction.
- Equipment worth 800 million naira for a modern palm oil mill is lying idle in the southeastern Cross River state because of disagreement within the state government on who should install them.
- Interest rates have continued to fall with deposit rates down to as low as five percent from 15 percent last year when rates were uncapped.
- Appeal court rules that chairman of anti-narcotics agency has no power to shut any firm following case of two motor dealers whose businesses were closed on suspicion of money laundering.
